text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-The state competition council is investigating possible illegal price cooperation between petrol companies after a price war between petrol stations came to a sudden stop.
-After losing a shipbuilding contract worth 200 million pounds to competitor GEC Marine, Norway's Kvaerner may have to close down Govan shipyard near Glasgow.
-Police in many counties will not be able to carry out traffic controls during Easter because of a lack of money. Sevral police stations have already spend their overtime-budget for 1997.

-Experts doubt that the gold find from the sunken Spanish ship La Capitana outside Equador is worth as much as 25-28 billion crowns. According to Equador's largest newspaper two companies claim the right to the find, one of them the Norwegian investment company La Capitana Invest.

-Norwegian forestry group Norske Skog will consider using foreign railway companies to transport timber. Norske Skog's Jan Reinaas says prices are to high at state-owned railway company NSB and that service is poor.
